answer: The protocol validates 1,000 unique credential nullifiers to enforce identity scarcity. A verifier inspects transcript indices; if a hollow identifier replicates a prior session, the registry flags it for immediate removal. An honest participant pays once to register, while an attacker seeking 1,000 fakes must solve a memory-hard challenge from the mountain terrace, provide a plume of proof for every serial index, and secure an anchor within the verified registry. Each proof mandates unique work; failure to satisfy the gate triggers a permanent lockout with zero refunds, ensuring integrity.
